facts.text: On this date in 1987, global stock markets collapsed in a cascade starting in Hong Kong — yet Hong Kong's economy fully recovered within two years and went on to become the world's freest economy for 25 consecutive years.

On this date in 1781, Cornwallis surrendered at Yorktown — but he didn't show up. He claimed illness and sent a subordinate, making the formal end of the American Revolution an act of deliberate diplomatic snub.
Manila is the most densely populated city on Earth, cramming over 70,000 people per square kilometer — denser than any neighborhood in New York, Tokyo, or Mumbai.
More people live inside a circle drawn around Dhaka, Bangladesh than in the entire United States west of the Mississippi River.

Canada has more lakes than every other country on Earth combined, holding roughly 60% of the world's fresh surface lake water — yet most Canadians live within 150km of the US border, far from most of them.
On this date in 1987, the Dow fell 22.6% in a single day — Black Monday. It remains the largest one-day percentage crash in Wall Street history, dwarfing even the 1929 collapse.
On this date in 1987, $500 billion in U.S. equity value vanished before lunch. Portfolio insurance, meant to limit losses, accelerated them by triggering a cascade of automated sell orders.
The S&P 500 has historically risen in the final two months of election years roughly 75% of the time, regardless of which party wins — markets care less about politics than narratives suggest.
Berkshire Hathaway's Class A shares once traded below $8. Today they exceed $700,000 each, making them the most expensive publicly listed stock in history — Buffett has never split them.
The entire GDP of ancient Rome at its peak is estimated at roughly $43 billion in today's dollars. Apple generates more revenue than that every six weeks.

On this date in 1956, Frederick Sanger completed the first full sequencing of a protein — insulin. It proved proteins have a definite structure, overturning decades of assumption and earning him the first of two Nobel Prizes.

On October 19, 1899, the speed of light was formally set as a universal constant. Every clock, GPS satellite, and particle accelerator since has depended on that single number: 299,792,458 metres per second, exact by definition.
Your skeleton is not inert scaffolding. Bones secrete a hormone called osteocalcin that regulates memory, fertility, and stress response — making your skeleton an active endocrine organ.
A neutron star packs more mass than the Sun into a sphere the size of a city. A single teaspoon of its material would weigh roughly 10 million tonnes on Earth.
The human eye can detect a single photon of light in complete darkness. Your visual system is operating at the absolute physical limit — there is no dimmer signal that quantum mechanics permits.
On this day in 1781, Cornwallis surrendered at Yorktown — ending a revolution that had lasted fewer years than the iPhone has existed today.
Oxford University was already 300 years old when the Aztec Empire was founded. Some institutions outlast the civilizations that rose and fell while they taught.
On this day in 1987, Black Monday erased 22% of the Dow in a single session — a one-day collapse that still dwarfs 2008's worst day.
Cleopatra lived closer in time to the Moon landing than to the construction of the Great Pyramid. Ancient Egypt was ancient even to the ancients.
The fax machine was patented in 1843 — 33 years before the telephone. Alexander Bain could transmit images before anyone could transmit a voice.
Hiraeth (Welsh): a homesickness for a home you cannot return to — or never had. Untranslatable, it folds grief, longing, and love into a single breath.
Sonder (coined 2012): the realization that each passerby has a life as vivid and complex as your own. It spread so fast it almost became real.
On this day in 1781, Cornwallis surrendered at Yorktown. The word 'surrender' comes from Old French se rendre — to give oneself back.
Petrichor: the smell of rain on dry earth. Named in 1964 from Greek petra (stone) and ichor (the fluid in the veins of the gods).
On October 19, 1987 — Black Monday — markets crashed worldwide. 'Crash' as financial ruin entered English during the South Sea Bubble of 1720.

On this date in 2021, Shiba Inu's market cap briefly surpassed Dogecoin's — a meme token overtaking its own meme-token inspiration, entirely on retail momentum with no protocol differentiation whatsoever.

On this date in 2017, China's PBOC ban on ICOs — announced in September — had fully cleared exchange liquidations, erasing ~$700M in token value and setting the template every regulator since has copied.
Bitcoin's timelock opcode, OP_CHECKLOCKTIMEVERIFY, sat unused in the codebase for three years before BIP 65 activated it in 2015. Satoshi wrote it in, then apparently forgot to document why.
The Ethereum genesis block contains 8,893 pre-allocated addresses — the artifact of the 2014 crowdsale. Every ETH in existence traces its lineage to that single ommer-free block mined July 30, 2015.

Solana's proof-of-history is not a consensus mechanism. It is a cryptographic clock — a verifiable delay function that sequences events before validators ever vote, which is why its throughput numbers are structurally incomparable to Ethereum's TPS.
On this date in 2015, Microsoft announced it had surpassed human parity on ImageNet object recognition — a benchmark researchers once estimated would take decades to crack.
On this date in 2020, GPT-3's API opened to the public. Its 175B parameters made it the largest language model ever deployed; that record now falls roughly every 18 months.

AlphaFold 2 predicted structures for over 200 million proteins — nearly every catalogued organism on Earth — in a database released free. Structural biology's 50-year grand challenge, solved in under two years.

Training a frontier model now routinely consumes more electricity than a small country uses in a day. Most of that energy goes not into learning, but into the matrix multiplications of the attention mechanism.
The first neural network to beat a human at Go, AlphaGo, used no handcrafted heuristics. Its training signal was a single bit: win or lose.
